name: Surface and Mesh Extraction
text:
# Surface and Mesh Extraction
Also called: Gaussian Mesh Extraction, 3DGS Meshing

## Overview
This family provides methods to convert trained [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) models into explicit polygonal meshes or segmented 3D structures. While 3DGS [1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md] represents scenes as implicit volumetric primitives, these methods extract surface geometry for downstream applications like simulation, [compression](#4-compression.md), or editing. They differ from sibling methods like [CoR-GS](1486-cor-gs.md) or [EffGS](3365-effgs.md) by focusing on geometric fidelity and structural [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) rather than rendering speed or training efficiency.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a trained set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives $\mathcal{G} = \{g_1, \dots, g_N\}$, where each primitive $g_i$ is defined by its center $\boldsymbol{\mu}_i$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$, opacity $o_i$, and [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) coefficients $\mathbf{c}_i$. The core challenge is bridging the gap between the volumetric, alpha-blended representation of 3DGS and the explicit, watertight nature of triangle meshes or discrete segment labels.

The shared mathematical foundation involves evaluating the spatial distribution of the Gaussians. For mesh extraction, this typically involves aggregating opacity or density values onto a discrete grid or calculating distances to existing geometry. For segmentation, it involves projecting 3D primitives into 2D image space to associate them with semantic labels. All methods assume the availability of the standard [3DGS rendering](#7155-rendering-implementation.md) pipeline to generate reference views or depth maps [1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].

## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md)
Extracts a mesh by building a volumetric density field from Gaussian opacities and applying marching cubes. It relies on opacity accumulation rather than signed distance functions. Choose this when a training-free, direct mesh extraction from an existing 3DGS model is required.

### [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md)
Connects a pre-existing 3D mesh with Gaussian splats by classifying them as tightly-bound or loosely-bound based on distance to the surface. It prunes occluded splats and aligns surface-aligned ones. Choose this when refining a mesh-initialized 3DGS model to reduce redundancy and improve surface adherence.

### [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md)
Segments 3D Gaussians by lifting 2D segmentation masks from reference views into 3D space using multi-view voting. It is training-free and relies on SAM. Choose this for partial scene editing or semantic decomposition without requiring learnable feature vectors.

## Background
The extraction of explicit geometry from 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) is a recent development following the introduction of 3DGS [1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md]. Early 3DGS models were purely implicit, making them unsuitable for applications requiring explicit topology. Methods like GOF [3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md] and MeshGS [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md] emerged to address this, leveraging the density properties of Gaussians or their initialization from mesh data. Segmentation methods like [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md] extend this by enabling semantic understanding of the extracted geometry.
